```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Audit code frequencies

`nis_audit_code_transition()` summarizes named code groups by period. The
example is a small invented data frame. When supplying prefixes directly,
use separate calls for ICD-9 and ICD-10.

```{r audit}
toy <- data.frame(
  YEAR = rep(2018:2020, each = 2),
  I10_DX1 = c("I5022", "E119", "I509", "E119", "I5022", "E119"),
  DISCWT = rep(1, 6)
)
nis_audit_code_transition(
  toy,
  codes = c(heart_failure = "I50", diabetes = "E11"),
  type = "dx"
)
```

The output gives unweighted and weighted group counts and each group's share
of all discharges within the period. A year-over-year percentage change is
relative to the prior observed period; it is descriptive and does not explain
why coding prevalence changed.

## Group by several period columns

`by` accepts more than one column. A period is then an observed combination,
such as year and quarter, sorted in the order given. A period with a missing
component is kept as its own row after the complete periods. No unambiguous
year comparison exists for several columns, so `yoy_pct_change` is `NA` in
every row; compare `pct_within_year` across the periods you choose.

```{r audit-by}
toy$DQTR <- rep(c(1L, 2L), times = 3)
toy$DQTR[6] <- NA
nis_audit_code_transition(
  toy,
  codes = c(heart_failure = "I50"),
  type = "dx",
  by = c(YEAR, DQTR)
)
```

## Inventory observed codes

`output = "inventory"` lists the full codes that matched each prefix group,
with counts for every period. `status` marks a code `absent` when a period has
no matches and `sparse` when its unweighted count is at most `sparse_n`
(default 10). A group that matches no observed code appears once per period
with a missing `code`. The counts are aggregate, so apply your disclosure
rules before sharing them.

```{r inventory}
nis_audit_code_transition(
  toy,
  codes = c(heart_failure = "I50", diabetes = "E11"),
  type = "dx",
  output = "inventory"
)
```

## Compare diagnosis positions

Principal and secondary diagnoses can capture different presentations.
`nis_audit_dx_position()` compares counts and selected outcome rates across
principal, secondary-only, and any-position definitions.

```{r sensitivity}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019))
nis_audit_dx_position(nis, "I50")
```

The rows show how the synthetic definition changes with diagnosis position.
These are descriptive weighted summaries, not survey estimates with standard
errors. Use a survey design for inferential comparisons.

## Handle the ICD transition

NIS changed from ICD-9-CM to ICD-10-CM/PCS in October 2015. 2015 combines
ICD-9 discharges from Q1–Q3 with ICD-10 discharges from Q4. For a query
containing both slot sets, supply the two definitions explicitly. Each
definition uses its own slots, version information, and eligible quarters.
These invented codes illustrate the syntax.

```{r mixed-flag}
nis_open(nis_example(years = 2015)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(flag = list(icd9 = "12345", icd10 = "I50"), system = "both") |>
  dplyr::count(DQTR, flag) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

Use a single-system call when only one slot set is present. Review clinical
equivalence and trends with the study's code sets. Mixed-system flags are
experimental.

## Reuse cohort criteria

Pass the `flow` from [the cohort example](cohorts.html#record-eligibility-across-the-2015-transition)
as `codes` to compare its any-slot and principal criteria by quarter. Each
criterion is counted independently within the audit denominator. This audit
uses all discharges in each period. Supply `cohort` to choose a different
denominator, for example adults with a known age.

```{r audit-flow, eval=FALSE}
attr(flow, "nis_criteria")
nis_audit_code_transition(nis, codes = flow, by = c(YEAR, DQTR))
```

For the invented example, any-slot counts in Q3 and Q4 are 24 and 19.
Principal counts are 9 and 18. A discharge matching several prefixes or
slots contributes once per criterion.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - A trend break can reflect code-set changes, case mix, or practice as well
>   as a true change in prevalence.
> - A zero in an audit means no match in the selected system, not absence in a
>   different code system.
> - An `absent` or `sparse` inventory status describes this dataset and cohort;
>   it does not show that a code is unused.
> - Principal and any-position summaries are nested definitions, not
>   independent groups.

To keep the flags for later analysis, call `nis_flag_dx()` once for each
position, then derive the mutually exclusive secondary-only flag.

```{r position-flags}
nis |>
  nis_flag_dx(hf_any = "I50") |>
  nis_flag_dx(hf_principal = "I50", position = "principal") |>
  dplyr::mutate(hf_secondary_only = hf_any & !hf_principal) |>
  dplyr::count(hf_principal, hf_secondary_only) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

See [`nis_audit_code_transition()`](../reference/nis_audit_code_transition.html)
and [`nis_audit_dx_position()`](../reference/nis_audit_dx_position.html).
